note: Spain with the land it held overseas (Spanish Sahara, Spanish Guinea; Morocco is in the France family), walked back from 2026.

reviewed.why: Spain with the Balearic and Canary Islands, Ceuta and Melilla
Western Sahara: Spanish Sahara until 1976, then held by Morocco west of its sand wall (and by Mauritania in the south until 1979)
Equatorial Guinea: Spanish Guinea (Fernando Po, Annobón and Río Muni) until 1968

changes.what: Mauritania gives up its part of Western Sahara under the Algiers agreement of 5 August 1979; Morocco takes Dakhla and annexes Western Tiris

hatch.note: Western Tiris (Tiris al-Gharbiyya), the southern third of Western Sahara, held by Mauritania from Spain's departure (partition treaty with Morocco of 14 April 1976) until it gave up its claim in August 1979

changes.what: Spain leaves Spanish Sahara under the Madrid Accords of November 1975, handing it to Morocco and Mauritania
Spanish Guinea becomes independent as Equatorial Guinea
